question: With whose participation did the Anushilan group join forces when the Bengal Congress broke up into two factions after the death of |CR Das ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**JM Sengupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Anushilan Samiti was a prominent revolutionary organization in Bengal during the early 20th century, known for its nationalist and anti-colonial activities.
 
• Following the death of CR Das in 1925, the Bengal Congress split into two factions: one led by Subhash Chandra Bose and the other by JM Sengupta.
 
• The Anushilan group aligned with the faction led by JM Sengupta, who was regarded as a moderate nationalist leader.
 
• JM Sengupta’s faction was more focused on constructive political strategies and less inclined towards radical measures compared to Bose’s faction.
 
• This collaboration between the Anushilan group and JM Sengupta’s faction aimed to strengthen nationalist efforts in Bengal during the critical phase of India's freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anushilan Samiti:** Founded in 1902, the Anushilan Samiti played a crucial role in revolutionary activities against British rule, focusing on militant nationalism.
 
• **CR Das:** Chittaranjan Das was a prominent nationalist leader, lawyer, and the founder of the Swaraj Party, advocating for self-rule and constitutional reforms.
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose:** Known as Netaji, he was a radical leader of the Indian National Congress and later formed the Indian National Army to fight British colonial rule.
 
• **Moderates vs. Extremists:** The early 20th-century Congress was divided into moderates, who sought gradual reforms, and extremists, who advocated for immediate independence through direct action.
 
• **Political Context:** The post-1925 period marked a significant shift in Bengal’s nationalist movement, with emerging factions influencing strategies and alliances in the fight against colonial rule.
